title: Attacks and Their Impact

header.html: 4.2 Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network: DoS and DDoS; VLAN hopping; MAC flooding; ARP poisoning and spoofing; DNS poisoning and spoofing; rogue devices and services (DHCP, AP); evil twin; on-path attack; social engineering (phishing, dumpster diving, shoulder surfing, tailgating); malware
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Network attacks

Attack What happens Impact
DoS / DDoS Floods a target so legitimate users cannot reach it; DDoS uses many sources (botnet) Availability lost
VLAN hopping Gets into another VLAN by switch spoofing (pretending to be a trunk) or double tagging Segmentation bypassed
MAC flooding Fills the switch's MAC table so it floods frames out every port Eavesdropping, switch acts like a hub
ARP poisoning / spoofing False ARP replies make hosts send traffic to the attacker's MAC On-path interception on the LAN
DNS poisoning / spoofing False DNS answers (or a poisoned cache) send users to the wrong IP address Redirection to fake sites
Rogue DHCP server Hands out wrong gateway or DNS settings Traffic redirected
Rogue access point An unauthorized AP connected to the network A backdoor into the LAN
Evil twin A fake AP copying a real SSID Credentials and traffic captured
On-path attack (formerly man-in-the-middle) The attacker sits between two parties and reads or changes traffic Confidentiality and integrity lost
Exam tip

. A switch flooding unknown frames out every port = MAC flooding. Wrong gateway handed to clients = rogue DHCP. A fake copy of the company Wi-Fi = evil twin.

2Social engineering and malware

Attack Meaning
Phishing Deceptive messages that trick users into revealing credentials or running malware
Dumpster diving Searching trash for sensitive information (shred documents)
Shoulder surfing Watching someone enter a password or read a screen (privacy screens)
Tailgating Following an authorized person through a secured door (mantraps, badge checks)
Malware Malicious software: virus, worm, ransomware, trojan, spyware

3Impact

Attacks hit confidentiality (data exposed), integrity (data altered) or availability (service denied). Defenses are covered in Module 19 (port security, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, segmentation, training).

Exam tip

. Layer 2 attacks (MAC flooding, ARP poisoning, VLAN hopping) happen inside the LAN; port security and 802.1X defend against many.

Exam tip

. Attacks aimed at availability (DoS, DDoS) are different from attacks that intercept (ARP poisoning, evil twin, on-path). Name the goal first.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A switch begins forwarding traffic out all ports after its MAC address table is filled with bogus entries. What attack is this?

  • AARP poisoning
  • BMAC flooding
  • CDNS poisoning
  • DVLAN hopping
Show the answer

Answer: B. MAC flooding exhausts the CAM table.

S2Users receive the wrong default gateway from an unknown device on the LAN. What is the likely cause?

  • AAn evil twin
  • BA rogue DHCP server
  • CA DNS recursive resolver
  • DMAC filtering
Show the answer

Answer: B. A rogue DHCP server hands out false settings.

S3Employees connect to a Wi-Fi network named like the company SSID, and their credentials are captured. What is this attack?

  • AA rogue DHCP server
  • BVLAN hopping
  • CAn evil twin
  • DA DDoS attack
Show the answer

Answer: C. An evil twin copies a legitimate SSID.

S4An attacker uses forged ARP replies to receive traffic meant for the default gateway. What type of attack results?

  • AA denial-of-service attack
  • BAn on-path attack
  • CA ransomware attack
  • DA DNS amplification attack
Show the answer

Answer: B. ARP poisoning places the attacker in the path.

S5An intruder follows an employee through a badge-controlled door. What is this?

  • AShoulder surfing
  • BDumpster diving
  • CPhishing
  • DTailgating
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tailgating is following an authorized person into a secured area.

S6Thousands of compromised devices flood a web server with requests. What attack is this?

  • AA distributed denial-of-service attack
  • BVLAN hopping
  • CARP spoofing
  • DDNS poisoning
Show the answer

Answer: A. Many sources attacking availability is DDoS.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does MAC flooding target?

Show the answer

The switch's MAC address table.

R2How does VLAN hopping work?

Show the answer

Through switch spoofing or double tagging.

R3What is an on-path attack?

Show the answer

An attacker positioned between two parties who reads or changes traffic.

R4What is dumpster diving?

Show the answer

Searching trash for sensitive information.

R5What is shoulder surfing?

Show the answer

Watching someone enter a password or read a screen.

R6What does a rogue AP create?

Show the answer

An unauthorized wireless backdoor into the network.
